sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a bi-weekly podcast from the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是一档由美国心理学会出品的每两周一期的播客节目。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Caitlin Luna.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯特琳·卢娜。

sentences.en: Buying has never been more convenient in America today.
sentences.zh: 在当今的美国，购物从未如此便捷。

sentences.en: If you're in a major metro area, you can have just about anything you want delivered right to your door within minutes or hours.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在主要大都市区，几乎任何你想要的东西都可以在几分钟或几小时内直接送到你家门口。

sentences.en: Clothes, groceries, fast food medicine, you don't even need to leave the house.
sentences.zh: 衣服、日用品、快餐、药品，你甚至都不用出门。

sentences.en: Yet at the same time, some Americans are moving toward a different path, decluttering their homes and lives, and adhering to lifestyles like minimalism
sentences.zh: 然而与此同时，一些美国人正走向一条不同的道路，他们精简自己的家和生活，并践行诸如极简主义等生活方式，

sentences.en: and financial independence retire early, also known as FIRE.
sentences.zh: 以及财务独立、提早退休，也被称为FIRE。

sentences.en: Why do some people buy so much while others shun that lifestyle for simplicity or to save?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人疯狂买买买，而另一些人则为了追求简约或省钱而避开这种生活方式？

sentences.en: How do brands reach into our psyches to get us to pull out our wallets and credit cards?
sentences.zh: 品牌是如何触及我们的心理，让我们掏出钱包和信用卡的？

sentences.en: What are some of the motivations behind companies that try to appeal to our sense of social responsibility to get us to spend?
sentences.zh: 那些试图通过迎合我们的社会责任感来让我们消费的公司，其背后有哪些动机？

sentences.en: Our guest for this episode is psychologist Dr. Kit Yarrow, an expert on consumer behavior and professor emerita at Golden Gate University in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们这期的嘉宾是心理学家基特·亚罗博士，她是一位消费者行为专家，也是旧金山金门大学的名誉教授。

sentences.en: She studies why and how people shop and buy and how companies can best meet consumer needs.
sentences.zh: 她研究人们购物和消费的原因与方式，以及公司如何最好地满足消费者的需求。

sentences.en: She's the author of Decoding the New Consumer Mind about the Motivations and Behaviors of Shoppers Today and Gen Buy about the Consumption Habits of Millennials.
sentences.zh: 她是《解码新消费心理：当今购物者的动机与行为》以及《消费一代：千禧一代的消费习惯》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Dr. Yarrow is regularly interviewed on national media, including Good Morning America, NPR, and USA Today.
sentences.zh: 亚罗博士经常接受国家级媒体的采访，包括《早安美国》、NPR和《今日美国》。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Yarrow.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，亚罗博士。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to have you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I'm excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Today's consumers, as I said, can get almost anything they want whenever they want.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，今天的消费者可以随时随地买到几乎任何他们想要的东西。

sentences.en: What is motivating consumer spending today?
sentences.zh: 是什么在激励着当今消费者的消费？

sentences.en: Well, you know, in some ways, it's the same as it's always been, that people need things, obviously, and shopping helps people prep for life transitions,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，在某些方面，这和过去没什么两样，人们显然需要东西，而且购物有助于人们为生活转变做准备，

sentences.en: like thinking about having a baby or moving and so on, and we just simply crave newness.
sentences.zh: 比如考虑生孩子或搬家等等，而且我们纯粹是渴望新鲜感。

sentences.en: So those are fairly constant, but I think what's different today is the triggers.
sentences.zh: 所以这些因素相当恒定，但我认为现在不同的是触发因素。

sentences.en: So never before, and I've been studying this for more than 20 years, have I seen people so attracted to bargains.
sentences.zh: 所以我研究这个已经超过20年了，我从没见过人们对大减价如此着迷。

sentences.en: So I think this fear of missing out, which we call FOMO in my field, is really motivating to shoppers.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种错失恐惧症，我们在我的领域称之为FOMO，对购物者来说真的非常有动力。

sentences.en: And it's detrimental, I think, to their financial help, that people get more excited about the bargain than they do about what it is they're actually buying.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这对比他们的财务健康是有害的，人们对打折商品的兴奋感超过了他们实际购买的东西本身。

sentences.en: The same kind of trigger of FOMO applies when you're on vacation, and so that's like, I have to get this here and now,
sentences.zh: 当你度假时，也会遇到同一种FOMO触发因素，这就好比，我此时此地必须买下这个，

sentences.en: otherwise I won't be able to get it later, or a limited time offer, limited quantity available.
sentences.zh: 否则我以后就买不到了，或者限时优惠、数量有限。

sentences.en: So these are the triggers, I think, that are a little bit different today than in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这些我认为就是与过去略有不同的触发因素。

sentences.en: In terms of some of the products that people are buying today that are relatively new, what I'm finding is that anxiety-reducing products are so big today.
sentences.zh: 就人们今天购买的一些相对较新的产品而言，我发现减压产品现在非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: So this is one of the big shifts as well, that CBD, sleep aids, Blu-ray glasses, a lot of these things, to me, just point out that we're an increasingly anxious society,
sentences.zh: 所以这也是巨大的转变之一，CBD、助眠剂、防蓝光眼镜，在我看来，很多这些东西都表明我们是一个日益焦虑的社会，

sentences.en: and people are gravitating towards whatever they think is going to help them fix their anxiety, heavy blankets and so forth.
sentences.zh: 人们倾向于任何他们认为能帮他们解决焦虑的东西，比如重力毯等等。

sentences.en: And the other thing people are looking for that's a little bit different than in the past is products that help or brands that help them feel connected to other people.
sentences.zh: 人们在寻找的另一类与过去略有不同的是能够帮助他们或品牌帮助他们感到与他人建立联系的产品。

sentences.en: So we've seen this big uprising in wanting to do business with companies that match your values.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到，想要与符合你价值观的公司做生意的愿望出现了一个大高潮。

sentences.en: We call it purpose marketing.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为宗旨营销。

sentences.en: And a lot of this is really related to, I think, a sense of kind of loneliness that people have, that they want to feel connected to other people,
sentences.zh: 我认为这在很大程度上与人们内心的一种孤独感有关，他们希望感到与他人有联系，

sentences.en: and they want to have experiences instead of just things.
sentences.zh: 并且他们希望拥有体验，而不仅仅是物品。

sentences.en: Yeah, just as you mentioned, many brands are going beyond that traditional advertising to take on social causes.
sentences.zh: 是的，正如你所提到的，许多品牌正在超越传统广告，承担起社会公益。

sentences.en: And a few notable examples that come to mind are Dove with its campaigns about challenging beauty stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 我想到的几个显著例子是多芬，它推出了挑战美丽刻板印象的活动。

sentences.en: We have the Gillette campaign that challenged toxic masculinity that was from earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 我们有吉列在今年早些时候开展的挑战有害男性气概的活动。

sentences.en: And Burger King recently came out with its Real Meals campaign that encourages people to feel their emotions and know that it's okay not to be okay.
sentences.zh: 汉堡王最近推出了“真实餐”活动，鼓励人们感受自己的情绪，并知道感觉不好也没关系。

sentences.en: Do you think those campaigns resonate with consumers and translate into sales more than ever before?
sentences.zh: 你认为这些活动能比以往更好地与消费者产生共鸣并转化为销量吗？

sentences.en: It depends on how well they're done.
sentences.zh: 这取决于它们做得有多好。

sentences.en: So, for example, the Gillette campaign that you mentioned,
sentences.zh: 比如，你提到的吉列活动，

sentences.en: the purpose of that campaign was to let people know that men can do better.
sentences.zh: 那个活动的目的在于让人们知道男人可以做得更好。

sentences.en: And really, people bristled at that one.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，人们对这个感到很生气。

sentences.en: They felt like Gillette, a big company, is telling me how to be a parent.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得吉列是一家大公司，却在教我怎么当父母。

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不对。

sentences.en: Whereas others, like Dove and REI, has had some campaigns that have resonated.
sentences.zh: 而其他的，比如多芬和REI，有一些活动引起了共鸣。

sentences.en: Nike's had campaigns that have resonated.
sentences.zh: 耐克也有引起共鸣的活动。

sentences.en: You know, it depends on how authentic they feel to the consumer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这取决于它们在消费者看来有多真实。

sentences.en: Sometimes they're not actually all that authentic.
sentences.zh: 有时候它们其实并不是那么真实。

sentences.en: Like Nike's championing of women at the same time that this very company, you know, has class discrimination suits against them by women.
sentences.zh: 比如耐克在大力支持女性的同时，这家公司本身却遭到女性的性别歧视诉讼。

sentences.en: And, you know, the irony of that, it's just that their campaign feels so authentic to consumers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其中的讽刺之处在于，只是他们的活动让消费者觉得太真实了。

sentences.en: It feels so genuine that it works.
sentences.zh: 它让人觉得如此真诚，所以管用了。

sentences.en: Because I think consumers today, they, you know, they don't trust business in general.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为今天的消费者，他们，你知道，总体上不信任商业。

sentences.en: So, what they are looking for is a peek inside the values of the company.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们在寻找的是对公司价值观的一窥究竟。

sentences.en: And if a company is really good at either genuinely communicating values, which I think is the case with Dove and REI,
sentences.zh: 如果一家公司非常擅长真诚地传达价值观，我认为多芬和REI就是这样，

sentences.en: or they're really good marketers like Nike, and it may not be genuine, but it looks that way to consumers, this feels good to them.
sentences.zh: 或者他们是非常出色的营销人员，比如耐克，虽然可能并不真诚，但在消费者看来是这样的，这让他们感觉很好。

sentences.en: People don't want to just buy products.
sentences.zh: 人们不只想买产品。

sentences.en: They want to buy a connection to the company in a sense that they're getting more than a product, that brands have to kind of go beyond profit as a reason for existing today.
sentences.zh: 他们想要买到与公司的联系，某种程度上他们得到的不仅仅是产品，品牌现在必须超越利润作为生存的理由。

sentences.en: It does seem like people want to, general consumers, want to align themselves more with brands.
sentences.zh: 看起来人们确实想要，普通消费者想要更多地与品牌保持一致。

sentences.en: I've heard people say that.
sentences.zh: 我听过人们这么说。

sentences.en: Like, they want to use a certain product maybe because it's environmentally friendly, or it's healthier, or non-GMO, or something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们想用某个产品，也许是因为它环保，或者更健康，或者非转基因，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yeah, it seems like that is something you do hear more often.
sentences.zh: 是的，这似乎确实是你更常听到的一种情况。

sentences.en: I can't say if that's more so than in the past, but it does seem like brands want to get more into the values each person holds today.
sentences.zh: 我不能说这是否比过去更多，但品牌似乎确实想要更多地切入每个人今天的价值观。

sentences.en: That's, yeah, it's definitely true.
sentences.zh: 那是，是的，这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, without a doubt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: I think partly because we have so many products, competition is huge.
sentences.zh: 我想部分是因为我们有太多的产品，竞争极其激烈。

sentences.en: And because I think people aren't connected through some of the old traditional ways that they connected through either religion or their community,
sentences.zh: 而且因为我认为人们没有通过他们过去通过宗教或社区联系的那些老传统方式联系在一起，

sentences.en: knowing people around them, you know, there's a sense of, I think, people wanting to belong to things
sentences.zh: 了解他们周围的人，你知道，我认为人们有一种归属感，

sentences.en: and wanting to connect to higher values beyond, you know, just what exists in their life.
sentences.zh: 并且想要连接到超越他们生活中现存事物的更高价值观。

sentences.en: And so brands can play this role, and brands make people feel like they're getting more than just products.
sentences.zh: 所以品牌可以扮演这个角色，品牌让人们觉得他们得到的不仅仅是产品。

sentences.en: And so without a doubt, if you can buy, you know, tomatoes from four different places, and, you know, one of them is a locally grown, you feel like you're supporting a, you know,
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，如果你可以从四个不同的地方买西红柿，其中一个地方是本地种植的，你觉得你是在支持一个，

sentences.en: an actual individual, and they aren't using chemicals, and they're contributing to schools and so forth,
sentences.zh: 真正的个人，而且他们不使用化学品，他们为学校做贡献等等，

sentences.en: you're going to buy those tomatoes instead of what, you know, you perceive to be mass-produced tomatoes.
sentences.zh: 你会买那些西红柿，而不是你认为是大规模生产的西红柿。

sentences.en: So, you know, a lot of times consumers are really making great decisions that help their communities, help their planet, help, you know, everything better.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，很多时候消费者确实在做伟大的决定，帮助他们的社区，帮助地球，帮助一切变得更好。

sentences.en: And then sometimes I have to say, you know, they're being manipulated that, you know, that GM, you know, some of the products that tout these all-natural characteristics
sentences.zh: 但有时我必须说，你知道，他们被操纵了，那些标榜这些纯天然特征的产品，

sentences.en: are really not any better for the environment, not any better for the individual.
sentences.zh: 其实对环境并没有更好，对个人也没有更好。

sentences.en: They're just using that as their showcase.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把这作为他们的展品。

sentences.en: It's just so much information for consumers, and frankly, nobody has time to evaluate all of it.
sentences.zh: 对消费者来说信息太多了，坦白说，没有人有时间去评估所有这些。

sentences.en: And so on the one hand, I think we have this opportunity to, you know, the old saying is vote with your wallet to, you know, to tout your values through what you buy.
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，我认为我们有机会，老话说得好，用你的钱包投票，通过你买的东西来宣扬你的价值观。

sentences.en: And on the other hand, it's a whole new opportunity to be manipulated by marketers.
sentences.zh: 而另一方面，这也是一个被营销人员操纵的全新机会。

sentences.en: I want to touch on some of those marketing techniques that work in a bit here, but I do want to mention something, go on something you talked about in your first answer
sentences.zh: 我一会儿想谈谈一些奏效的营销技术，但我确实想提一下，继续你第一个回答中谈到的内容，

sentences.en: about buying experiences.
sentences.zh: 关于购买体验。

sentences.en: So people are more, as you said, invested in buying an experience, like going on a trip or a concert or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，人们更多地投资于购买体验，比如去旅行、听音乐会或诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So are more people moving to that trend?
sentences.zh: 所以是不是更多的人正在转向这种趋势？

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, we always are attracted to scarcity.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们总是被稀缺性所吸引。

sentences.en: And what's scarce today, you know, is emotion and experience and a sense of purpose.
sentences.zh: 而今天稀缺的是情感、体验和目标感。

sentences.en: And, you know, what's abundant today are mass-produced products.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，今天丰富的是大规模生产的产品。

sentences.en: So what people used to want, you know, to showcase who they are to other people, to, you know, connect to something more, bigger, better,
sentences.zh: 所以过去人们想要的，为了向其他人展示他们是谁，为了连接到更宏大、更美好事物的东西，

sentences.en: was oftentimes a product, like a luxury product or a better product or more products.
sentences.zh: 往往是一个产品，比如奢侈品、更好的产品或更多的产品。

sentences.en: And now that that's no longer scarce, now that that's like so overwhelming, I mean, we're just bloated with products.
sentences.zh: 而现在这不再稀缺了，现在这让人应接不暇，我的意思是，我们满腹产品。

sentences.en: I think what people are looking for is the emotional intensity that they get from an experience.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们在寻找的是他们从体验中获得的情感强度。

sentences.en: And then some of the benefits that people got from products, the emotional benefit of showing other people who you are through what you have, which has been throughout time.
sentences.zh: 然后是人们从产品中获得的一些好处，通过你拥有的东西向其他人展示你是谁的情感好处，这一直存在。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not new.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不新鲜。

sentences.en: You know, or, you know, showing that you're in a special class of people through a product, you know, that sort of became gauche and tacky after the recession.
sentences.zh: 你知道，或者，通过产品展示你属于一个特殊的阶层，你知道，这在经济衰退后变得有点俗气和不得体。

sentences.en: But people can still do that by showing off what they buy through their social media accounts, the experiences they buy, I mean.
sentences.zh: 但人们仍然可以通过在社交媒体账号上炫耀他们买的东西，也就是他们买的体验，来做到这一点。

sentences.en: So you can't exactly put your new shoes on social media and say, look at me, I'm so cool.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能把你的新鞋发到社交媒体上说，看我，我多酷。

sentences.en: But you can put your trip to Thailand on there and it does, it kind of accomplishes the same thing, but it doesn't feel quite as tacky.
sentences.zh: 但你可以把去泰国的旅行发上去，这确实，它起到了类似的作用，但感觉没那么俗气。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And how does social media influence buying?
sentences.zh: 社交媒体是如何影响购买的？

sentences.en: Well, I think a lot of people make a, you know, make some buying decisions because of social media that are not always in their best intereSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为很多人因为社交媒体而做出的一些购买决定并不总是符合他们的最大利益。

sentences.en: So, for example, I found that when people constantly come in contact with products because it's in their social media feed,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，我发现当人们不断接触产品，因为它们在他们的社交媒体信息流中，

sentences.en: they develop this sense of familiarity with those products that makes them feel like they can have them.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些产品产生了一种熟悉感，让他们觉得自己可以拥有它们。

sentences.en: And it stops them from going through the rational decision-making process of wondering, do I really want it?
sentences.zh: 这阻止了他们经历理性的决策过程，去想：我真的想要它吗？

sentences.en: Can I afford it?
sentences.zh: 我买得起吗？

sentences.en: Does it fit into my lifestyle?
sentences.zh: 它符合我的生活方式吗？

sentences.en: Am I going to use it?
sentences.zh: 我会用它吗？

sentences.en: It just sort of becomes part of their life in a kind of like creepy sideways kind of way.
sentences.zh: 它只是以一种诡异的、旁敲侧击的方式成为了他们生活的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, and by the same token, what also happens is I think when you see your friends have particular products
sentences.zh: 你知道，同样地，发生的事情还有，我认为当你看到你的朋友拥有特定的产品，

sentences.en: or have remodeled and they have these new kitchen things or, you know, whatever these products are or fancy vacations, it seems like it's a new kind of peer pressure, I think.
sentences.zh: 或者重新装修了并且有了这些新的厨房用品，或者无论这些产品是什么，或者是豪华假期，这似乎是一种新的同辈压力。

sentences.en: Another way I think social media affects us negatively in terms of purchasing is that, you know, we only have so much resilience.
sentences.zh: 我认为社交媒体在购买方面对我们产生负面影响的另一种方式是，你知道，我们的恢复力是有限的。

sentences.en: So, when we're constantly stalked by something, maybe we looked at, you know, maybe we went to a website and we saw a product and we thought about it, decided not to.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们不断被某样东西纠缠时，也许我们看过了，也许我们去了一个网站，看到了一个产品，考虑了一下，决定不买。

sentences.en: Well, the next thing you know, wherever you go online, that product follows you around.
sentences.zh: 好吧，紧接着你会发现，无论你在网上走到哪里，那个产品都对你穷追不舍。

sentences.en: You know, it just pops up in your feed or it pops up as an ad on a, you know, magazine site that you're reading.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它只是弹出来在你的信息流里，或者作为你正在阅读的杂志网站上的广告弹出来。

sentences.en: And so, people will say no only so many times and then they're more likely to cave in.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们说不的次数是有限的，然后他们更有可能屈服。

sentences.en: So, all of these things I think contribute to people making purchases that maybe they wouldn't have made were it not for our online lives and very specifically also social media.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些事情，我认为都导致人们进行了可能在没有我们的网络生活、特别是社交媒体的情况下不会进行的购买。

sentences.en: Is that one of the reasons why people buy things they don't need?
sentences.zh: 这是人们购买他们不需要的东西的原因之一吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure many people out there have bought something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我相信外面的很多人都买过东西。

sentences.en: It's now still sitting in the closet with the tags on, collecting duSt.
sentences.zh: 它现在还挂着标签躺在衣柜里，积着灰尘。

sentences.en: It probably should be donated.
sentences.zh: 它大概应该被捐掉。

sentences.en: Is that why people, why this happens?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们，为什么会发生这种事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, it's one of the reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是原因之一。

sentences.en: This is actually something I found in my research was that in all the homes I go to,
sentences.zh: 这其实是我在研究中发现的一点，在我去过的所有家庭中，

sentences.en: so what I usually do is an ethnography, which means that I go in people's houses and I look in their closets
sentences.zh: 我通常做的是民族志研究，这意味着我走进人们的家里，查看他们的衣柜，

sentences.en: and under their beds and the backs of their freezers and, you know, depending on the product I'm researching or the category I'm researching.
sentences.zh: 看他们的床底下和冰柜后面，你知道，这取决于我正在研究的产品或类别。

sentences.en: But all of a sudden, I noticed like, wow, it's not just me or this woman or that guy.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间我注意到，哇，不仅仅是我、这个女人或那个家伙。

sentences.en: It's freaking everybody that has clothes they haven't worn in their closets or products they haven't used in the back of their sinks, in the back of their bathroom sinks.
sentences.zh: 简直是所有人，衣柜里都有没穿过的衣服，或者浴室水槽后面有没用过的产品。

sentences.en: And I thought, you know, why is that?
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，为什么会这样？

sentences.en: So, I kind of made that like an added part of my research, a personal intereSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我把这当作我研究的一个补充部分，一个个人兴趣。

sentences.en: And I found that a lot of it has to do with what I call faulty thinking, that somebody will fall in love with an item.
sentences.zh: 我发现这在很大程度上与我所说的错误思维有关，即某人会爱上一件物品。

sentences.en: Clothing is the easiest, I think, to look at.
sentences.zh: 我认为衣服是最容易查看的。

sentences.en: So, they fall in love with an item and they, you know, really want to have it, but it's too expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以他们爱上了一件物品，你知道，真的很想拥有它，但太贵了。

sentences.en: And then it goes on sale, but it didn't go on sale on their size.
sentences.zh: 然后它打折了，但没有打他们那个尺码的折。

sentences.en: So, they buy it anyway, kind of thinking maybe it will.
sentences.zh: 所以他们还是买了，心里想着也许会有。

sentences.en: Or it's not quite their right color, you know.
sentences.zh: 或者颜色不太对，你知道。

sentences.en: So, it's the product they wanted, but it's like maybe yellow and yellow is not their color.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们想要的产品，但也许是黄色的，而黄色不是他们的颜色。

sentences.en: So, they buy it anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以他们还是买了。

sentences.en: So, it has like one thing wrong with it, but everything else is right with it.
sentences.zh: 所以它有一点不对劲，但其他一切都对。

sentences.en: And they kind of, you know, rationalize going ahead and buying it.
sentences.zh: 他们某种程度上为继续购买合理化了。

sentences.en: And another thing that happens is that people sort of have this fantasy life that they're imagining.
sentences.zh: 另一件发生的事情是，人们脑海中有一种虚构的生活在想象中。

sentences.en: So, you know, a lot of people buy clothes that are too small for them, thinking that they're going to get thinner.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，很多人买对他们来说太小的衣服，认为自己会变瘦。

sentences.en: And then, you know, what happens is they get thinner and they don't actually like what their skinny self picked out.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，发生的事情是他们变瘦了，但他们其实并不喜欢变瘦后的自己挑中的东西。

sentences.en: They want to, you know, that skinny self wants to pick out their own things, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们想要，你知道，那个瘦了的自己想要挑自己的东西。

sentences.en: Or it didn't fit or they never do get slim or, you know, they imagine like they're going to be going on cruises or things that don't happen.
sentences.zh: 或者尺寸不合适，或者他们根本没有变瘦，或者，你知道，他们想象自己要去游轮或不会发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, they have clothing to match a life that they don't actually have now and then it doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拥有的衣服是为了他们现在实际上并没有的生活准备的，然后并没有发生。

sentences.en: And another reason that I found that people buy things they don't actually end up wearing is because, and this is going to sound really silly, but I heard this over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我发现人们买东西但最终没穿的另一个原因是，这听起来真的很傻，但我一次又一次地听到这个。

sentences.en: They love it so much.
sentences.zh: 他们太喜欢了。

sentences.en: They're afraid something will happen to it.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕它出什么问题。

sentences.en: So, they're like saving it.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们就像是把它珍藏起来。

sentences.en: They save and save and save and it just sits there and they're waiting for just the right occasion.
sentences.zh: 他们存了又存，存了又存，它就那样摆在那儿，他们一直在等一个最合适的时机。

sentences.en: And there's some reason why any occasion isn't good enough.
sentences.zh: 而且总有各种理由觉得任何时机都不够完美。

sentences.en: They could spill, the right people aren't going to see them in it and on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 可能会弄脏，合适的人没看到他们穿着它，诸如此类，没完没了。

sentences.en: And they don't actually wear these things because they love them too much.
sentences.zh: 结果他们其实根本不穿这些东西，因为他们太喜欢了。

sentences.en: Last reason, incredibly common, especially now that we're shopping online, drunk shopping or high shopping.
sentences.zh: 最后一个原因，极其常见，特别是现在我们都在网上购物，也就是酒后网购或者嗨了以后网购。

sentences.en: So, I have some of my favorite consumer stories are people that bought like very outrageous things and then they go, see, this is what happens when you shop when you're high.
sentences.zh: 所以，我最喜欢的一些消费者故事就是，有人买了极其离谱的东西，然后他们会说，看吧，这就是你嗨的时候网购的下场。

sentences.en: And so, my advice in all of these is don't buy anything you can't return and, you know, that'll solve a lot of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，我对所有这些情况的建议是，不要买任何不能退货的东西，你知道的，这能解决很多问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's better to stay away from the phone, the Amazon one click away if you've been under the influence or are not.
sentences.zh: 对，最好还是远离手机，远离亚马逊的一键下单，不管你当时是不是神志不清。

sentences.en: Maybe a little sleep deprived, whatever that might be.
sentences.zh: 也许有点睡眠不足，不管是什么情况吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, what are some of those basic human impulses and insecurities that companies try to appeal to to get us to buy?
sentences.zh: 那么，公司为了吸引我们购买，会利用哪些基本的人性冲动和不安全感呢？

sentences.en: I know we've talked about anxiety, but what others do you think marketers look at and say, okay, let's try to sell our product by appealing to people in this way or that way?
sentences.zh: 我知道我们聊过焦虑，但你认为营销人员还会关注哪些其他心理，并觉得，好吧，让我们通过这种或那种方式吸引人们来推销我们的产品？

sentences.en: You know, I think, I think the bargain thing is really what companies rely on.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我觉得，我认为打折这个噱头确实是公司最依赖的。

sentences.en: It's their and it's their Achilles heel too because their margins are decreased when they try to sell everything on sale anyway.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们的软肋，因为无论如何，当他们试图通过打折销售所有东西时，他们的利润率就会下降。

sentences.en: But it works with consumers and that's why they do it.
sentences.zh: 但这对消费者很管用，这就是他们这么做的原因。

sentences.en: So, a lot of a lot of stores actually stock their shelves with merchandise that they never really anticipate they'll sell for full price,
sentences.zh: 所以，很多很多商店实际上都在货架上摆满了一些他们根本没指望能按原价卖出去的商品，

sentences.en: knowing that consumers will buy it when it's reduced.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道消费者会在降价时购买。

sentences.en: So, you know, it makes sense to me that consumers wait for bargains or they're inspired by bargains.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，在我看来，消费者等待打折或受到打折的启发，这是合乎情理的。

sentences.en: I think we don't trust that we understand the value of a product inherently.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们从根本上不相信自己能理解一件产品的价值。

sentences.en: And so, we rely on price to tell us if we're getting a good deal or if we're getting ripped off or, you know.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们依赖价格来告诉我们自己是捡到了便宜，还是当了冤大头，你知道的。

sentences.en: And we also, I think, intuitively kind of understand that when it's on sale, it probably won't last as long.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们也在某种程度上凭直觉理解，当商品打折时，它可能不会维持太久。

sentences.en: So, it motivates us to take action immediately.
sentences.zh: 所以，这促使我们立即采取行动。

sentences.en: But in the end, what I find is that people really spend way too much time kind of thinking about that price and they aren't thinking about the product.
sentences.zh: 但到头来，我发现人们确实花太多时间去考虑价格，而没有去考虑产品本身。

sentences.en: In an ideal world, what I'd love to see is consumers just look at the product, not even look at the price, decide if they like it or not, and then look at the price.
sentences.zh: 在理想情况下，我最想看到的是消费者只看产品，甚至不看价格，先决定自己是否喜欢，然后再看价格。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: and I think people would end up with more products that they enjoy that are actually really satisfying to them so that they ultimately spend less money and buy fewer products.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们最终会买到更多他们真正喜欢的、能让他们真正满意的产品，这样他们最终花的钱反而更少，买的产品也更少。

sentences.en: A lot of the products that people buy, you know, they don't like, they don't end up using, they're not satisfying, they don't get a thrill from, and so they end up buying more.
sentences.zh: 人们买的很多产品，你知道的，他们并不喜欢，最后也没用，根本无法满足他们，也带不来什么刺激，所以他们最后反而买得更多了。

sentences.en: And we can solve that problem, I think, if people are really much more careful about examining the product and thinking hard about what they want to add to their life.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能更加仔细地审视产品，并认真思考自己到底想把什么带进生活中，我想这个问题就能得到解决。

sentences.en: The other kind of tricks I think that we see marketers using today that maybe were less popular 10 years ago is this concept of something being reinvented.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们今天看到的另一种营销人员使用的套路，在十年前可能没那么流行，那就是“重新发明”这个概念。

sentences.en: So, our use of technology, I think, has made us really love innovation and newness.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为我们对科技的使用，让我们对创新和新鲜感爱不释手。

sentences.en: And so, when we think that something's been reinvented, we get all excited about it and, you know, we want to learn more about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们认为某样东西被“重新发明”时，我们就会为此兴奋不已，并且，你知道的，想要了解更多。

sentences.en: So, you know, especially online and especially in social media, we learn about reinvented shoes and reinvented jewelry and cars and bras and you name it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，特别是在网上，特别是在社交媒体上，我们了解到被重新发明的鞋子、被重新发明的珠宝、汽车、胸罩，等等等等。

sentences.en: And, frankly, a lot of these products are not reinvented.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，很多这样的产品根本没有被重新发明。

sentences.en: The distribution system is reinvented or maybe one aspect of it is reinvented or there's more transparency.
sentences.zh: 分销系统被重新发明了，或者说它的某一个方面被重新发明了，又或者是透明度更高了。

sentences.en: But it's not necessarily a product benefit.
sentences.zh: 但这不一定算得上是产品本身的优势。

sentences.en: So, consumers get very excited about this idea that they're supporting maybe a small new company.
sentences.zh: 因此，消费者对这种自己可能是在支持一家小型新兴公司的想法感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: But it may not be the best product for them.
sentences.zh: 但这可能并不是最适合他们的产品。

sentences.en: It may not be the right choice for them.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是他们的正确选择。

sentences.en: It certainly, a lot of times, is not the best price.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，它绝对不是最好的价格。

sentences.en: But they fall for it.
sentences.zh: 但他们还是上钩了。

sentences.en: And, again, partly because of the social media stuff, you know, that it stalks them and so on.
sentences.zh: 而且，再次说明，部分原因是因为社交媒体之类的东西，你知道的，它像影子一样缠着你，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But partly because I think we really fall for the whole concept of it being reinvented.
sentences.zh: 但部分原因我认为是我们真的很容易被“重新发明”这个整体概念所迷惑。

sentences.en: And then maybe one other is how we pay for things.
sentences.zh: 然后可能还有另一个因素，那就是我们支付的方式。

sentences.en: So, the more detached we are from actual money that we're earning, that we're giving up to pay for something,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们离自己赚到的、为了支付某样东西而放弃的实际金钱越远，

sentences.en: the easier it is for us to overspend and even potentially go into debt.
sentences.zh: 我们就越容易过度消费，甚至可能陷入债务危机。

sentences.en: So, if everybody really thought about how many hours they had to work in order to get this particular product or what they're giving up, you know, if I get this, oh,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果每个人都认真想想，为了买到这件特定的产品，自己必须工作多少个小时，或者自己放弃了什么，你知道的，如果我买了这个，哦，

sentences.en: that's one-tenth of a vacation I was thinking of.
sentences.zh: 那相当于我原本计划的度假费用的十分之一。

sentences.en: Or, oh, geez, I had to work eight hours in order to get that much money to pay for that.
sentences.zh: 或者，哦天哪，我得工作八个小时才能赚到那么多钱来付这个账。

sentences.en: So, I think if we were much more aware of the exchanges we're making for things that we buy, we would buy better things and probably fewer things.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为如果我们对我们为所购物品做出的交换有更多意识，我们就会买到更好的东西，而且可能买得更少。

sentences.en: So, you know, how do you do that?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，怎么做到这一点呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think every time we use easy payment, you know, the credit card is already loaded in the computer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想每次我们使用便捷支付时，你知道的，信用卡已经在电脑里绑定好了。

sentences.en: So, we just have to press a button.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们只需按一下按钮就行了。

sentences.en: This gives us fewer seconds to actually make those – to have those thoughts of, oh, geez, you know, if I get that, I won't be able to get this.
sentences.zh: 这留给我们去实际做出——去产生那些想法的时间就更少了：天哪，你知道的，如果我买了那个，我就买不了这个了。

sentences.en: Or, oh, man, that's a big chunk of change, you know, and I only have this much.
sentences.zh: 或者，哦天哪，这是一大笔钱，你知道的，而我只有这么多。

sentences.en: You know, and that's what we really want to do is think about the impact of that purchase on our financial health and security and, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这正是我们真正想要做的，去思考这次购买对我们的财务健康和安全的影响，你知道的，

sentences.en: and other things that we might want to buy and need.
sentences.zh: 还有我们可能想要购买和需要的其他东西。

sentences.en: Do you think that means people are spending more because of online shopping?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是否意味着人们因为网上购物而花得更多了？

sentences.en: Well, we are seeing credit card debt go back up again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实看到信用卡债务在回升。

sentences.en: I mean, that's partly because banks are loosening up their requirements.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这部分是因为银行正在放宽申请要求。

sentences.en: We saw it dip really nicely after the recession, and for a while there, economists were kind of thinking, oh, look at us.
sentences.zh: 我们在经济衰退后看到它大幅下降，有一段时间经济学家还在想，哦，看看我们。

sentences.en: We're all being so well-behaved.
sentences.zh: 我们表现得都这么乖。

sentences.en: But it might have been that we couldn't get any credit.
sentences.zh: 但那可能只是因为我们根本贷不到款。

sentences.en: But in general, we are seeing debt levels rise again, which probably indicates that people are spending money more easily.
sentences.zh: 不过总的来说，我们确实看到债务水平再次上升，这可能表明人们花钱变得更容易了。

sentences.en: And we definitely are seeing people shop for products more easily online.
sentences.zh: 而且我们绝对看到人们在网上购买产品变得更加轻而易举。

sentences.en: But there's kind of like two different kinds of ways that people shop.
sentences.zh: 但人们购物的方式大致有两种不同的类型。

sentences.en: I don't think brick and mortar – I hate that term.
sentences.zh: 我不认为实体店——我讨厌这个词。

sentences.en: You know, physical retail, I don't think that's going away.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，实体零售，我不认为它会消亡。

sentences.en: I think there's, you know, there's pitfalls to both, and people do enjoy shopping in both arenas for different reasons.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道的，这两种方式都有各自的缺陷，人们出于不同的原因确实都很享受在这两个领域购物。

sentences.en: Are you more likely to impulse buy in person or online?
sentences.zh: 你更容易在实体店还是网上冲动消费？

sentences.en: I think you impulse buy pretty equally in both.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你在两者的冲动消费程度其实差不多。

sentences.en: Online, the thing that gets people to impulse buy is other – you know, it's just so well done.
sentences.zh: 在网上，促使人们冲动消费的原因是其他——你知道的，它做得太出色了。

sentences.en: When websites – you pick out your product, it goes in your basket, and then up comes – other shoppers also looked at this, and you get new ideas.
sentences.zh: 当网站上——你挑选了你的产品，它进入了你的购物车，然后就会弹出——其他购物者也看了这个，然后你就会获得新的灵感。

sentences.en: Or, you know, if you buy this one too, then you can get free shipping.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，如果你也买这个，就能享受包邮。

sentences.en: You know, our shipping threshold is X amount.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的起运额度是X金额。

sentences.en: And, oh my gosh, people spend a lot of money to get free shipping or a free offer.
sentences.zh: 然后，天哪，为了包邮或者免费赠品，大家会花很多钱。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you spend $100 on cosmetics, then you get this bag of cosmetics for free.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你花100美元买化妆品，就能免费得到这包化妆品。

sentences.en: And then, you know, a lot of times people will buy things they don't need.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，很多时候人们会买一些不需要的东西。

sentences.en: And most of the time, those are kind of impulse purchases, and so are the add-on purchases.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数时候，这些都是冲动消费，附加商品也是如此。

sentences.en: Just like in stores, what I found is that if people haven't made a commitment to buy anything, they're much better at analyzing the products they're considering buying.
sentences.zh: 就像在实体店里一样，我发现如果人们还没有承诺购买任何东西，他们就更擅长分析自己考虑购买的产品。

sentences.en: Once they make a commitment to buy something, they're just wide open to making mistakes.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们承诺购买某样东西，他们就完全敞开了犯错的大门。

sentences.en: So that's why, you know, the classic example is the candy at the register at the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么，你知道，最经典的例子就是杂货店收银台的糖果。

sentences.en: But, you know, all stores have thought about what people will see in the checkout line in stores and know that they are selling a lot of merchandise.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，所有商店都考虑过顾客在结账排队时会看到什么，并且知道他们正在售出大量商品。

sentences.en: As people have made a commitment to buy, they know they're going to get out their wallet, their credit card, whatever, and now they're open to buying more.
sentences.zh: 当人们已经承诺购买时，他们知道自己要掏出钱包、信用卡之类的东西，现在他们愿意买更多了。

sentences.en: And the same thing happens online, that once people make a commitment to buy, they're open to buying more.
sentences.zh: 网上也是一样，一旦人们承诺购买，他们就愿意买更多。

sentences.en: So, in general, I would say, you know, good shopping would be for consumers, again,
sentences.zh: 所以，总的来说，我认为，你知道，对消费者而言，好的购物方式再次是

sentences.en: to kind of pull back and reevaluate every single product they're considering buying and to be wary of the add-on buy.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上收缩并重新评估他们考虑购买的每一件产品，并对附加购买保持警惕。

sentences.en: That's the most dangerous impulse buy is the add-on buy.
sentences.zh: 那是危险的冲动购物，就是附加购买。

sentences.en: How do we resist that?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何抵制这一点？

sentences.en: Because that always happens when you're at the line, you know, say of like a Bed Bath & Beyond, and you're sneaking through the line.
sentences.zh: 因为当你排队时总是会发生这种情况，你知道，比如在Bath & Beyond这类店排队，你正在队伍里穿行。

sentences.en: There's all these little things you don't need, but, oh, maybe I do need that.
sentences.zh: 有所有这些你不需要的小物件，但是，哦，也许我确实需要呢。

sentences.en: Or there's candy.
sentences.zh: 或者有糖果。

sentences.en: Or you said, you know, you're served ads again.
sentences.zh: 或者正如你所说，你知道，你又看到了广告。

sentences.en: If you search for something online, any website you go to, you see it again.
sentences.zh: 如果你在网上搜索了什么，你去任何网站，都会再次看到它。

sentences.en: And how do you resist that and not fall for it?
sentences.zh: 你该如何抵制并不上当？

sentences.en: I mean, of course we know, okay, I shouldn't be spending the money on that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们当然知道，好吧，我不应该把钱花在那个上面。

sentences.en: I don't need this extra thing, but it's hard.
sentences.zh: 我不需要这个多余的东西，但这很难。

sentences.en: This is a really good time to check your email on your phone or pick up your novel where you left off on your phone.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝佳的时机，可以在手机上查邮件，或者在手机上接着读你的小说。

sentences.en: So, you know, for all the negatives in terms of consumption that technology has brought to us, maybe one of the positives is a little bit of a distraction.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，就科技给我们消费带来的所有负面影响而言，也许其中一个积极方面就是有一点分散注意力。

sentences.en: But with absolutely everything, you know,
sentences.zh: 但对于绝对所有事情，你知道，

sentences.en: the best thing people can do is make a list of what it is that they want to add to their life and understand why and not deviate from that liSt.
sentences.zh: 人们能做的最好的事情就是列一张清单，写下他们想要给生活添加什么，明白原因，并且不要偏离这张清单。

sentences.en: So that means that, you know, you're not going to even consider things that are, you know,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，你知道，你甚至不会考虑那些，你知道，

sentences.en: in the checkout line because they're not something that you determined beforehand were going to be part of your purchasing that day.
sentences.zh: 在结账队伍里的东西，因为它们不是你事先决定那天要购买的部分。

sentences.en: It sounds really harsh, like, oh, you can't have fun of just adding in, like, some lipstick or something.
sentences.zh: 听起来真的很严苛，就像，哦，你不能享受随便加一枝口红之类的乐趣。

sentences.en: I mean, why not?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And, you know, generally speaking, because I think you're going to enjoy that product more if it's something you set out to buy and considered than if you just throw it in later.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，总的来说，因为我认为如果那是你精心挑选并考虑购买的东西，你会比随便扔进购物车更享受那个产品。

sentences.en: These are so often – and this is, like, really proven in my research.
sentences.zh: 这些通常——这在我的研究中真的得到了证实。

sentences.en: Well, you know, when I talk to people about what they get pleasure from and, you know, where their dollars were most well spent,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，当我跟人们聊起他们的快乐源泉，以及，你知道，他们的钱花得最值的地方时，

sentences.en: never does it come up that it was the thing they threw in at the end.
sentences.zh: 从来没有哪个是最后随手扔进去的东西。

sentences.en: It doesn't.
sentences.zh: 根本没有。

sentences.en: So these are not satisfying and gratifying purchases.
sentences.zh: 所以这些并不是令人满意和满足的消费。

sentences.en: And so I say, you know, to have in your mind what it is that you are setting out to buy and stick to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，你知道，心里要清楚自己打算买什么，并且坚持下去。

sentences.en: That's a great idea.
sentences.zh: 这真是个好主意。

sentences.en: Is this why we hear people say, like, you know, I went to Target to buy two things and I spent $100?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们经常听到有人说，你知道，我本来去塔吉特（Target）只买两样东西，结果花了100美元？

sentences.en: That happens to me all the time at Costco.
sentences.zh: 我在好市多（Costco）也总是这样。

sentences.en: I look at my bill and I'm like, oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 我看着账单心想，哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's usually things I do need, but it's sort of shocking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通常都是我确实需要的东西，但还是有点震惊。

sentences.en: Sometimes you walk in there like, oh, I'm just going to get some groceries and I walk away with, like, a shower caddy, some new towels.
sentences.zh: 有时候你走进去，心想，哦，我只是去买点杂货，结果却带走了一个浴帘置物架、几条新毛巾。

sentences.en: Oh, boy.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think pretty much all of us have been in that boat before.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我们几乎所有人都曾有过这种经历。

sentences.en: You mentioned Target and Costco because some retailers have so earned our trust that they actually are places where we do allow ourselves to be more open.
sentences.zh: 你提到了塔吉特和好市多，因为一些零售商赢得了我们的信任，以至于它们确实成了我们允许自己更加随性的地方。

sentences.en: Probably more than any other place is Costco.
sentences.zh: 可能比任何其他地方都要数好市多。

sentences.en: But Target, I hear also from consumers that we kind of allow ourselves to be a little bit, you know, curious about what they have to offer.
sentences.zh: 但塔吉特也是，我从消费者那里听说，我们允许自己对他们提供的商品表现得有点，你知道，好奇。

sentences.en: We're sampling products.
sentences.zh: 我们在试用产品。

sentences.en: You know, we're introduced to new things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们接触到新事物。

sentences.en: We get new ideas.
sentences.zh: 我们获得了新灵感。

sentences.en: The stores cover our entire lifestyle from, you know, our lives, everything from what we wear to what we eat.
sentences.zh: 这些商店涵盖了我们的整个生活方式，从，你知道，我们的生活，从我们穿的到我们吃的，无所不包。

sentences.en: And so, you know, there's a lot of possibilities.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，有很多可能性。

sentences.en: So, honestly, I don't get as many complaints from consumers about bad purchase decisions made in those particular stores as I do when they're in a department store, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以，老实说，消费者对我抱怨在这些特定商店做出糟糕购买决定的次数，并不像他们在百货公司那样多，例如，

sentences.en: or on Amazon or, you know, another different type of retailer.
sentences.zh: 或者在亚马逊上，或者，你知道，其他不同类型的零售商。

sentences.en: So, but nevertheless, people do make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管如此，人们还是会犯错。

sentences.en: And the ones that I hear about the most are that they buy too much.
sentences.zh: 我听到最多的错误就是他们买得太多。

sentences.en: So, they're at Costco and they say, well, you know, that's only $5 for, you know, twice as much as we would spend to get, you know, at a regular grocery store.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们在好市多，然后他们会说，好吧，你知道，只多花5美元就能买到我们在普通杂货店买的两倍分量，

sentences.en: What a deal.
sentences.zh: 多划算啊。

sentences.en: And so, they buy much more, a much higher quantity of a product than they will actually use, you know, or worst case scenario,
sentences.zh: 于是，他们买得更多，购买的数量远超他们实际会消耗的，你知道，或者最糟糕的情况是，

sentences.en: they buy a lot more of a product that's not good for them like cookies and then they do use it.
sentences.zh: 他们买了很多对他们身体不好、比如饼干之类的大量产品，然后他们真的把它们吃掉了。

sentences.en: So, there's something about like, well, I like to see, I always like to see people using math.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有点像，嗯，我喜欢看，我总是喜欢看人们在算账。

sentences.en: So, but they're kind of calculating that they're getting three times as much for only twice as much in dollars and they fall for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，但他们盘算着只多花两倍的钱就能买到三倍的分量，然后他们就上当了。

sentences.en: Again, it's the bargain thing that gets people every time, you know, and the danger there is that they don't use it or that they use it and they probably shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，正是这种便宜货总能吸引人，你知道，那里的危险在于他们不用它，或者他们用了但本不该用。

sentences.en: But I think also sampling creates a sense of obligation.
sentences.zh: 但我认为试吃也会产生一种义务感。

sentences.en: So, when somebody gives you something, you feel like you should really consider it.
sentences.zh: 所以，当别人给你一些东西时，你会觉得你真的应该考虑一下。

sentences.en: Whereas maybe, you know, gummy vitamins were sort of not on your liSt.
sentences.zh: 而也许，你知道，软糖维生素本来不在你的清单上。

sentences.en: But because you got one, you tasted it, it tasted good and you could, you know, what's wrong with vitamins?
sentences.zh: 但因为你拿到了一个，尝了尝，味道不错，而且你还可以，你知道，维生素有什么不好的？

sentences.en: You end up buying it.
sentences.zh: 你最终还是买下了它。

sentences.en: So, you get new ideas and then you get this sense of obligation and then the price point's usually good.
sentences.zh: 所以，你得到了新灵感，然后产生了一种义务感，而且价位通常也不错。

sentences.en: And so, you know, again, I think just people have to try to stick to their list as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，再说一次，我认为人们必须尽量紧跟自己的购物清单。

sentences.en: There are a few places, I think, where people don't get into quite as much trouble deviating from their liSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在少数几个地方，人们在偏离购物清单时不会陷入太大的麻烦。

sentences.en: And maybe those are a couple of them.
sentences.zh: 也许其中就有几个。

sentences.en: Is that one of those techniques we were just talking about that a physical store might use?
sentences.zh: 这会不会是我们刚才讨论的实体店可能会使用的方法之一？

sentences.en: You said samples, you know, it does make you feel like, oh, maybe I should buy that because this nice person gave me this.
sentences.zh: 你提到了样品，你知道的，这确实会让人觉得，哦，也许我应该买这个，因为这个好心人给了我这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, samples definitely work.
sentences.zh: 对，对，样品绝对管用。

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的天哪。

sentences.en: And, you know, even sampling like any sort of sense of obligation.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，甚至连样品也会带来某种负债感。

sentences.en: So, you might have noticed that in a lot of department store now, people ask you if you would like some water when you're shopping.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能已经注意到，现在很多百货公司里，当你购物时，人们会问你想不想喝点水。

sentences.en: And that makes you feel, just that one water makes you feel much more open and receptive to buying.
sentences.zh: 这就让你觉得，仅仅是这一瓶水，就让你对购买表现得更加开放和接受。

sentences.en: And I think for a lot of consumers, customer service is so bad and they feel so mistreated when they go shopping that if they're just treated nicely,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，对很多消费者来说，客户服务太糟糕了，他们在购物时觉得自己受到了不公的对待，所以如果有人只是友好地对待他们，

sentences.en: they want to buy something just to kind of like vote in favor of that store.
sentences.zh: 他们就会想买点东西，权当是为那家店投赞成票。

sentences.en: So, you know, our social norms of, you know, reciprocity, you know, sometimes, I mean, in some ways it's a wonderful thing and in other ways, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们的社会规范，你知道的，互惠，你知道的，有时候，我的意思是，在某些方面这是一件好事，但在另一些方面，你知道的，

sentences.en: it can cost you money and to just be aware of it that, you know, that that that water comes with a little bit of a price tag attached to it, even if it's free.
sentences.zh: 它可能会让你花钱，只要意识到这一点，你知道的，那瓶水其实是带有一定价格标签的，哪怕它是免费的。

sentences.en: And on the flip side of that, I'm assuming because this happens that it does work when ads are served to you again and again and you see this product again.
sentences.zh: 反过来看，我假设既然这种情况确实会发生，那么当广告一次又一次地推送给你，让你再次看到这个产品时，它确实是管用的。

sentences.en: Does, is that proven to, to work to get people to then make a purchase?
sentences.zh: 这真的被证明管用，能促使人们下单购买吗？

sentences.en: Well, so there's kind of like a rule in advertising that people don't hear or see an ad the first time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以在广告界有一个类似这样的规则，那就是人们第一次听到或看到广告时并不会真正注意到。

sentences.en: It takes like a few times, like at least three times before people generally like get the gist of what you're selling.
sentences.zh: 通常需要好几次，至少三次，人们才会大致明白你在卖什么。

sentences.en: But if you see it over and over and over again, probably they didn't have enough advertisers because, well, yeah, what we found over and over and over again on TV,
sentences.zh: 但如果你一遍又一遍、反反复复地看到它，可能是因为他们的广告商不够，因为，好吧，我们在电视上反反复复看到的情况，

sentences.en: I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 我说的是这个。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Because generally what happened, what has happened there is that they didn't get enough variety of advertisers and, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为通常发生的情况是，那里没有提供足够多的广告商种类，而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: they're just bonusing those spots to their advertiser that they do have.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把这些广告位当作赠品送给他们现有的广告商。

sentences.en: And consumers actually find that incredibly annoying and it, and it backfires.
sentences.zh: 而消费者实际上觉得这极其烦人，而且，而且会适得其反。

sentences.en: It is very annoying when you see the same thing again, you're like, I've watched this commercial forever.
sentences.zh: 当你再次看到同样的东西时真的很烦人，你会想，我都看这个广告一辈子了。

sentences.en: Horrible.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: Are we more influenced by people we don't know, like celebrities or, you know, strangers who review something on Amazon or people who do product reviews on YouTube?
sentences.zh: 我们是更容易受到我们不认识的人的影响，比如名人，或者，你知道的，在亚马逊上写评论的陌生人，或者是YouTube上做产品评测的人？

sentences.en: Are those people more influential to us than say a family member or a friend in terms of buying?
sentences.zh: 就购物而言，这些人比我们的家人或朋友更有影响力吗？

sentences.en: No, no, for sure.
sentences.zh: 不，不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: The family members and friends are number one.
sentences.zh: 家人和朋友永远排在第一位。

sentences.en: They have been for all time.
sentences.zh: 过去一直是这样。

sentences.en: They probably will be for all time.
sentences.zh: 可能永远都会是这样。

sentences.en: So somebody that you actually know and trust is number one.
sentences.zh: 所以你真正认识并信任的人才是第一位的。

sentences.en: But number two are people you perceive to be like you.
sentences.zh: 但排在第二位的是那些你觉得和你相似的人。

sentences.en: So that's why reviews on websites where they break down age, for example, or, you know, skin tone, if you're looking at cosmetics or where people live, you know,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有些网站的评论会按年龄细分，或者，你知道的，如果你在看化妆品，会按肤色细分，或者按人们居住的地方细分，你知道的，

sentences.en: you see that you can filter out the reviewer according to other criteria.
sentences.zh: 你会发现你可以根据其他标准来筛选评论者。

sentences.en: This makes those reviews much more credible.
sentences.zh: 这使得这些评论具有更高的可信度。

sentences.en: Now, so we're looking – so first of all, to answer your question, family and friends come first and then people we perceive to be like us, everybody else has fallen off.
sentences.zh: 好了，所以我们在看——首先，回答你的问题，家人和朋友排在第一位，然后是我们觉得和自己相似的人，其他所有人都不太行了。

sentences.en: So when people do trust barometers, what we found is trust in government, trust in businesses, trust in even NGOs, nonprofit organizations,
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们做信任度晴雨表时，我们发现对政府的信任、对企业的信任、甚至对非政府组织、非营利组织的信任，

sentences.en: really trust across the board has diminished for consumers.
sentences.zh: 消费者对各行各业的信任度确实都在下降。

sentences.en: Consumers feel really burdened by having to figure out everything themselves because they don't trust these social establishments that are there supposedly to serve them.
sentences.zh: 消费者觉得自己背负着沉重的负担，必须自己弄清楚一切，因为他们不信任这些本该为他们服务的社会机构。

sentences.en: And they're looking for trustworthy sources of information because really, who can possibly do all the research, right?
sentences.zh: 他们在寻找值得信赖的信息来源，因为说实话，谁能把所有的研究都做一遍呢，对吧？

sentences.en: So enter now the Instagrammer, the YouTuber, the blogger that appears to be like them and appears to have like great deep knowledge of a particular subject matter,
sentences.zh: 于是，Instagram博主、YouTuber、博主登场了，他们看起来和他们一样，并且似乎对某个特定主题有很深厚的专业知识，

sentences.en: whether it's home improvement or makeup or something like that.
sentences.zh: 不管是家居装修、化妆还是类似的事情。

sentences.en: And those people become in a way kind of like a friend or family member, you know,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这些人变得有点像朋友或家人，你知道的，

sentences.en: you can develop a level of intimacy or a feeling of intimacy with them that allows their recommendations to carry almost as much weight as somebody that you actually know.
sentences.zh: 你可以与他们建立某种程度的亲密感，或者产生亲密的感觉，这使得他们的推荐几乎和那些你真正认识的人分量相当。

sentences.en: So I think what we're finding, though, in the review world is that, you know, this is so new.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们在评论界发现的是，你知道的，这太新了。

sentences.en: I mean, when you think about it, it's really a new field.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仔细想想，这真是一个全新的领域。

sentences.en: And now the system is being gamed so much.
sentences.zh: 而现在这个系统被严重操纵了。

sentences.en: So many of the reviews on Amazon are not authentic and on other websites.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊和其他网站上的许多评论都不是真实的。

sentences.en: And so consumers are learning that they can't always trust the reviews anymore.
sentences.zh: 因此消费者们正在了解到他们不能总是相信网上的评论了。

sentences.en: And they're discovering ways of trying to figure out who's authentic and who's not, like verified purchasers and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他们正在摸索各种方法来弄清楚谁是真实购买者，谁不是，比如通过已验证的购买者等等。

sentences.en: And what are some of the shopping and money mistakes you see people often make?
sentences.zh: 你认为人们经常犯的购物和金钱错误有哪些？

sentences.en: I think we've touched on a few, but can you elaborate on that a little more?
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经谈到了一些，你能再详细阐述一下吗？

sentences.en: Well, first and foremost, it's being overly focused on bargains.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先也是最重要的是过度关注打折和便宜货。

sentences.en: So not paying enough attention to the product and whether that's the right one for you and really getting way too excited about how much you're so-called saving by buying something.
sentences.zh: 所以没有花足够多的心思去关注产品本身以及它是否真的适合你，反而为通过买东西所谓的“省了多少钱”而感到过分兴奋。

sentences.en: The second one, I think, is getting, you know, obsessed with whether or not you're getting a return on your time investment.
sentences.zh: 第二个，我认为是变得，你知道的，执着于你是否获得了时间投资的回报。

sentences.en: So this is especially true, I think, when people shop in outlet malls.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为当人们在奥特莱斯购物时，这一点尤其明显。

sentences.en: They'll drive some length of time and they feel like because they spent so much time getting somewhere, well, they're just going to have to get something.
sentences.zh: 他们开车花了一段时间，觉得自己既然花了那么多时间来到这里，好吧，那就无论如何都得买点东西。

sentences.en: And the same is true, I think, when people are shopping online.
sentences.zh: 我想当人们在网上购物时也是如此。

sentences.en: If they spend a significant amount of time looking for something, they sort of feel like they have to get something back for that time investment.
sentences.zh: 如果他们花了大量时间寻找某样东西，他们就会觉得必须从这种时间投资中得到点什么回报。

sentences.en: Not having enough pain of payment, I like to call it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把它叫做缺乏付款的痛苦。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think when people can really easily purchase things, this allows them to buy more than they probably should.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我认为当人们可以非常轻松地买东西时，这会让他们买下比他们本来应该买的更多的东西。

sentences.en: And maybe the best example there is when people take Uber and Lyft.
sentences.zh: 也许最好的例子就是人们乘坐Uber和Lyft的时候。

sentences.en: I found that a lot of shoppers, a lot of the consumers I've spoken with sort of look at it like a free ride, you know,
sentences.zh: 我发现很多购物者，我交谈过的很多消费者，都把它看作是一次免费的行程，你知道的，

sentences.en: and then the credit card bills comes and they've spent way more than they thought they would on transportation.
sentences.zh: 然后信用卡账单来了，他们发现在交通上花的钱远远超过了他们的预期。

sentences.en: Because there's, you know, they just get out of the car and they don't have any sort of pain of payment.
sentences.zh: 因为有，你知道的，他们只是下了车，完全没有任何付款的痛苦。

sentences.en: You know, in general,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，总的来说，

sentences.en: what we want is people to really carefully analyze all the money that leaves their possession and think about whether or not they're giving up something important by making that purchase or how hard it was to earn money to make that purchase.
sentences.zh: 我们希望人们能够真正仔细地分析所有离开自己掌控的资金，并思考通过这次购买是否放弃了什么重要的东西，或者为了这次购买赚钱有多么辛苦。

sentences.en: And that doesn't happen as easily when people are being able to just press a button or get out of a car and make a purchase.
sentences.zh: 而当人们能够轻而易举地按个按钮或者下车就能完成购买时，这种思考就不会那么容易发生了。

sentences.en: I think buying more than you need is another mistake that people make.
sentences.zh: 我认为买超出需求的东西是人们犯的另一个错误。

sentences.en: So this could be buying, you know, too big of a quantity at Costco or it could be, you know, getting that extra color of something when, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是，你知道的，在Costco买太多分量的东西，或者可能是，你知道的，当黑色穿在你身上很好看时，你却去买了一种额外的颜色，结果买成了黄色，而你从来不穿那件黄色的。

sentences.en: if it looked good on you in black, then you get it in yellow too and you never wear the yellow one.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，我发现人们经常犯的一个错误是他们在孩子身上花太多钱。

sentences.en: And then, you know, I find that one of the mistakes that people make very often is they just spend too much money on their kids.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为这是陪伴他们的一种替代方式。

sentences.en: You know, I think it's a substitute for spending time with them.
sentences.zh: 实际上，你给孩子买的任何东西，都比不上一个无债一身轻、快乐的你，以及有时间陪伴他们的你。

sentences.en: And there's really nothing that you can buy a kid that's better than a happy you being debt free and having time to spend with them.
sentences.zh: 真正好的。

sentences.en: I want to turn now to what I mentioned at the top of the show about people who are on the other side of the coin.
sentences.zh: 接下来我想把话题转向我在节目开头提到过的人，也就是硬币的另一面。

sentences.en: So let's say, let's start with people who want to declutter their lives, which is really the antithesis of the consumer economy.
sentences.zh: 比如说，我们先从那些想要精简生活的人开始聊起，这其实与消费经济是完全对立的。

sentences.en: They want to get rid of things.
sentences.zh: 他们想要摆脱物品。

sentences.en: Why do you think people want to pare down the items they own?
sentences.zh: 你觉得为什么人们想要削减他们拥有的物品？

sentences.en: Well, I think we're just bloated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我们只是太臃肿了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we've had this huge influx of incredibly cheap merchandise coming in a lot from China, a lot.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，我们迎来了大量极其便宜的商品涌入，其中很多来自中国，真的非常多。

sentences.en: You know, the cost of products today has gone way down, and there's great abundance of cheap merchandise, mass-produced merchandise available.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如今产品的成本已经大幅下降，而且有大量廉价商品、批量生产的商品可供选择。

sentences.en: And consumers have, you know, stuffed their closets, stuffed their shelves, and it doesn't feel good.
sentences.zh: 消费者呢，你知道的，塞满了他们的衣柜，塞满了他们的书架，但这感觉并不好。

sentences.en: We don't feel good.
sentences.zh: 我们感觉不好。

sentences.en: Managing products makes us feel uncomfortable, makes us feel burdened.
sentences.zh: 管理产品让我们感到不舒服，让我们感到有负担。

sentences.en: And so I think this movement towards decluttering and really thinking about the Marie Kondo effect, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种走向精简的趋势，以及真正考虑近藤麻理惠效应，你知道的，

sentences.en: really thinking about the products that give you pleasure and whether or not you want them in your lives, in concept, this is terrific,
sentences.zh: 真正思考那些能带给你快乐的产品，以及你是否希望它们出现在你的生活中，从概念上讲，这太棒了，

sentences.en: will make people feel so much better to be very, very conscious about what they would like to have in their life and get rid of the things that they don't want in their life,
sentences.zh: 会让人们对自己在生活中想要什么有非常非常清晰的意识，并摆脱那些他们不想要的东西，

sentences.en: you know, donate them and so forth.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，把它们捐赠出去等等。

sentences.en: So all this is wonderful.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都很好。

sentences.en: I think it's a terrific movement.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个了不起的运动。

sentences.en: I think it absolutely makes sense from the perspective of how bloated most consumers feel and how overpurchased most people are in all income levels, by the way.
sentences.zh: 我认为从大多数消费者的臃肿感以及各个收入阶层的人过度购买的角度来看，这绝对是合情合理的，顺便说一句。

sentences.en: I'm not just talking about wealthy people here.
sentences.zh: 我这里不只是在谈论有钱人。

sentences.en: The only problem I have is that what I see is that people declutter and that they buy more stuff.
sentences.zh: 我唯一的疑问是，我看到的情况是人们精简了物品，然后他们又买更多的东西。

sentences.en: So for some consumers, not all, I mean, some people declutter and then they're really pleased with their, you know, more carefree life.
sentences.zh: 所以对于某些消费者来说，不是全部，我是说，有些人精简了物品，然后他们真的对他们那种，你知道的，更无忧无虑的生活感到高兴。

sentences.en: I mean, it just feels clean and healthy and it's easier.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这感觉很干净、很健康，而且更容易。

sentences.en: It takes less time to manage your life when you have fewer things in it.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有的东西变少时，管理生活所需的时间就更少了。

sentences.en: But then I would say there's a good, healthy proportion of people that then sort of fill up those shelves again, almost intuitive, almost instinctively.
sentences.zh: 但接着我要说，有相当一部分人随后几乎是凭直觉、几乎是本能地再次填满那些书架。

sentences.en: And that's where the problem arises.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: So I would say in terms of people who want to declutter their lives on a more extreme end, there's people who consider themselves minimaliSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，就那些想要更极端地精简生活的人而言，有些人认为自己是极简主义者。

sentences.en: So they only own things they need.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只拥有他们需要的东西。

sentences.en: You know, you hear about people who have only 10 items of clothing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你听说过有人只有10件衣服。

sentences.en: They live in very Spartan living conditions.
sentences.zh: 他们生活在非常简朴的居住条件下。

sentences.en: What do you, why do you think this appeals to people?
sentences.zh: 你觉得，为什么这会吸引人？

sentences.en: You know, I think in general, what we're seeing through the declutter movement, through the minimalist, through the fire movement, I think in all of these situations,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为总的来说，我们通过精简运动、通过极简主义、通过FIRE运动所看到的一切，我认为在所有这些情况下，

sentences.en: what we're seeing is a reaction to an unhealthy aspect of our, of our culture.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是对我们文化中不健康方面的一种反应。

sentences.en: That, that people, there's a backlash to overconsumption.
sentences.zh: 那就是，人们对过度消费产生了一种强烈反弹。

sentences.en: People feel like it's bad for our environment.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得这对我们的环境有害。

sentences.en: It's bad for our psyches, that it takes up too much of our time.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的心理有害，它占据了我们太多的时间。

sentences.en: And so in a variety of different ways, people are looking for solutions to that.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们正在以各种不同的方式寻找解决这一问题的办法。

sentences.en: Like how, how can they more consciously and live a life where consumption is based on need and not knee jerk or wants?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们如何才能更有意识地生活，让消费基于需求而不是膝跳反射般的冲动或欲望？

sentences.en: And then what about people who are a part of that fire movement, I said?
sentences.zh: 那么那些参与我刚才提到的FIRE运动的人呢？

sentences.en: So that's defined as financial independence, retire early.
sentences.zh: 这被定义为：经济独立，提前退休。

sentences.en: So those people are not spending much because maybe they're opting to buy used clothing, ride a bike instead of taking a car and saving most of the money they earn.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人花钱不多，因为他们可能选择买二手衣服，骑自行车而不是开车，并把赚到的大部分钱存起来。

sentences.en: Is that a popular movement?
sentences.zh: 这是一个受欢迎的运动吗？

sentences.en: Is it pervasive enough to be called a movement?
sentences.zh: 它是否已经普及到可以被称为一场运动的程度？

sentences.en: And do you think, what are some positives and negatives to it?
sentences.zh: 你认为它有哪些积极和消极的方面？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it is pervasive enough to be called a movement and it is really the extreme of the decluttering and, and the minimalist movement.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为它已经普及到可以被称为运动的程度，它确实是精简和极简主义运动的极端形式。

sentences.en: But in this case, they're also hoping to not have to work.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，他们还希望不必工作。

sentences.en: So they have not found satisfaction through employment and they want to be financially independent.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有在工作中找到满足感，他们想要实现财务独立。

sentences.en: And so, you know, part of their decision to decrease their spending and look for alternative ways to get their needs met is, you know, perhaps to declutter, perhaps, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他们决定减少支出并寻找替代方法来满足需求的决策的一部分，你知道的，可能是为了精简，可能是，你知道的，

sentences.en: to improve the environment, but also because they don't want to have to work.
sentences.zh: 为了改善环境，但也是因为他们不想工作。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, you know, there are like all these really creative ways to get what you need.
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，你知道，有很多非常创造性的方法来获取你所需的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, Goodwill and secondhand stores are just bulging and, you know, you really can, you really can get a lot of what you need without new manufacturing taking place and,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，旧货店和二手店人满为患，你知道的，你真的可以，你真的可以在没有新制造发生的情况下获得很多你需要的东西，

sentences.en: you know, borrowing things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，借用物品。

sentences.en: This has been a movement like to co-own products or borrow things.
sentences.zh: 这一直是一种像共同拥有产品或借用物品一样的运动。

sentences.en: There's all these ways that we can consume less and add fewer products to the world.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多方法可以减少消费，减少向世界添加产品。

sentences.en: But working in and of itself for a lot of people provides like a tremendous sense of connection to others and a tremendous gratification of having purpose and, you know,
sentences.zh: 但对很多人来说，工作本身能带来一种巨大的与他人连接感，以及拥有目标和巨大满足感，

sentences.en: an impetus, I think, to create things that a lot of people, I think, would feel would be missing.
sentences.zh: 我想，这也是创造事物的动力，很多人会觉得如果失去这个会有所欠缺。

sentences.en: You know, in some of the high wealth individuals I've interviewed, you know, one of their great fears, for example,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在我采访过的一些高净值个人中，你知道，他们最大的恐惧之一，举个例子，

sentences.en: is that they were to die young and give their kids too much money and an inheritance, that they would lose their interest in working, which a lot of people feel like is, you know,
sentences.zh: 就是如果他们英年早逝，给孩子留了太多钱和遗产，孩子们就会失去工作的兴趣，很多人觉得这是，你知道的，

sentences.en: a great source of pride and accomplishment and contribution to the community.
sentences.zh: 自豪感、成就感以及对社区贡献的巨大来源。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's pros and cons and trades-offs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，有利有弊，也有权衡。

sentences.en: I'm sure plenty of people in the FIRE movement are finding really productive things to do in their community.
sentences.zh: 我确信FIRE运动中的许多人正在他们的社区里做着非常富有成效的事情。

sentences.en: And, I mean, certainly they found creative ways to get their needs met.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，他们当然找到了创造性的方法来满足他们的需求。

sentences.en: So, hopefully their creativity is extending in a way where they feel purposeful and connected to others.
sentences.zh: 所以，希望他们的创造力能以这样一种方式延伸：让他们感到有目标感并与他人保持联系。

sentences.en: Yeah, I've done some research into that area.
sentences.zh: 是的，我围绕这个领域做了一些研究。

sentences.en: And it seems like a lot of people are saying maybe getting out of that, you know, rat race, if you will, and doing work they enjoy.
sentences.zh: 看起来很多人都在说，也许可以摆脱那种，你知道的，所谓的名利场（rat race），去做他们喜欢的工作。

sentences.en: Also, just being free from debt seems like a big motivating factor is just to not be, you know, chained down to an expensive mortgage, cars, and various things like that.
sentences.zh: 此外，仅仅摆脱债务似乎也是一个很大的动因，就是不再被，你知道的，昂贵的按揭贷款、汽车以及各种诸如此类的事情所束缚。

sentences.en: Or, you know, some people do also seem maybe driven by the environmental impact, as you mentioned, too.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，正如你刚才提到的，有些人似乎也受到环境影响的驱使。

sentences.en: So, yeah, being free from debt, you know, whether your goal is to not have to work or whether your goal is to just not have a credit card payment, I am all for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，摆脱债务，你知道的，无论你的目标是不必工作，还是仅仅不用支付信用卡账单，我都举双手双脚赞成。

sentences.en: That is such a psychological burden.
sentences.zh: 那真是一种沉重的心理负担。

sentences.en: So, one of my mantras, you know, whenever I'm hoping to help consumers buy better is that there's nothing you can buy, nothing you can own,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的座右铭之一，你知道，每当我希望能帮助消费者更好地购买时，那就是没有什么东西是你买得起、没有什么东西是你拥有的，

sentences.en: that will make you feel better than not having debt.
sentences.zh: 能比没有债务更能让你感觉良好。

sentences.en: So, you know, debt is such a burden.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，债务真是一个沉重的负担。

sentences.en: And usually the things you're buying are not, you know, equal or better than that debt,
sentences.zh: 通常你买的东西并不，你知道的，等同于甚至好过那种债务，

sentences.en: which means that you just walk around with a source of psychological negativity in your life,
sentences.zh: 这意味着你的生活中总是带着一个心理负能量的源头四处走动，

sentences.en: and you would actually be a happier person skipping that purchase and not having that debt.
sentences.zh: 而如果你省下那笔购买、没有这笔债务，你其实会是一个更快乐的人。

sentences.en: Now, that's obviously for discretionary purposes.
sentences.zh: 当然，这显然是指可自由支配的开支。

sentences.en: Some people go into debt for other reasons, but, you know, debt is an emotional burden.
sentences.zh: 有些人因为其他原因陷入债务，但是，你知道，债务是一种情感负担。

sentences.en: And, you know, the less debt you have for, you know, whether or not you, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，你身上的债务越少，不管你是不是，你知道的，

sentences.en: save really hard and pay off your mortgage as quickly as possible or avoid buying a car using debt, but, you know,
sentences.zh: 无论是咬牙攒钱并尽快还清房贷，还是避免贷款买车，但是，你知道的，

sentences.en: wait or get a used car or wait until you can afford one to buy it completely.
sentences.zh: 等一等，或者买辆二手车，或者等到你买得起的时候再全款买下。

sentences.en: All of these things will make you happier.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都会让你更快乐。

sentences.en: Than debt.
sentences.zh: 比起背负债务。

sentences.en: And how does your work influence your buying behaviors?
sentences.zh: 那么你的工作是如何影响你的购买行为的？

sentences.en: You know so much.
sentences.zh: 你知道得太多了。

sentences.en: Well, you know, I think I got interested in this initially.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我想我最初对这个产生兴趣。

sentences.en: Like, partly because I've always been interested in retail, but partly because I really do.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为我一直对零售业感兴趣，但部分原因是因为我是真的。

sentences.en: I'm basically cheap at heart.
sentences.zh: 我骨子里其实是个很抠门的人。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm just cheap.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我就是很抠。

sentences.en: And, you know, I thought it was a fun game when I was younger to figure out how to get more for less.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我年轻的时候觉得弄清楚怎么花更少的钱买到更多东西是个很好玩的游戏。

sentences.en: And then ultimately, you know, I enjoyed sharing this with other people.
sentences.zh: 到头来，你知道的，我很享受与其他人分享这一点。

sentences.en: So my mom told me once after I got started actually doing my own research, she said,
sentences.zh: 所以在我开始自己做研究之后，我妈妈有一次对我说，她说，

sentences.en: this is so funny because I remember at the grocery store once we were standing in line and you were looking in the cart ahead and you go, hey, mom,
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了，因为我记得有一次在杂货店排队时，你看着前面购物车里的东西说，嘿，妈妈，

sentences.en: how come those people have diet soda and cheesecake?
sentences.zh: 为什么那些人买减肥苏打水和芝士蛋糕？

sentences.en: So kind of a basic little kid question.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是小孩子会问的简单问题。

sentences.en: But I think I've always been interested in what people, how what people buy says about who they are and what it says about the world that we live in, too.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得我一直对人们买的东西、人们购买的东西如何反映他们是谁以及它如何反映我们所处的世界感兴趣。

sentences.en: I'm a pretty I'm not a good example because I'm a pretty cheap person by name.
sentences.zh: 我其实算不上一个好榜样，因为我本身就是一个挺抠门的人。

sentences.en: Not cheap, like cheap with my friends.
sentences.zh: 不是那种抠门，不是对朋友小气。

sentences.en: But I don't like I never really liked debt.
sentences.zh: 而是我不喜欢——我从来都不怎么喜欢债务。

sentences.en: I don't I don't even have a mortgage.
sentences.zh: 我甚至连房贷都没有。

sentences.en: I hate debt.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌债务。

sentences.en: I, you know, I feel cleaner and safer with it.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道的，背上没有债务让我觉得更清爽、更有安全感。

sentences.en: But I like I appreciate what shopping brings to our life and what product brings to our life.
sentences.zh: 但我喜欢——我很感激购物给我们生活带来的东西，以及产品给我们生活带来的东西。

sentences.en: And I just feel like if you analyze where you get the most joy and pleasure and really think about that and not be afraid to spend money where, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且我只是觉得，如果你分析一下自己从哪里获得了最多的快乐和愉悦，并真正去思考这一点，不要害怕把钱花在，你知道的，

sentences.en: it's meaningful to you and then avoid spending it because other people are because you feel like you should have it or, you know, because it's on sale.
sentences.zh: 对你来说有意义的地方，然后避免因为别人也在花、或者因为你觉得你应该拥有它、或者你知道因为在打折而盲目消费。

sentences.en: Like you're just a just a happier person overall.
sentences.zh: 这样总体来说你会成为一个更快乐的人。

sentences.en: And I do try to shop like that.
sentences.zh: 而且我也确实在努力这样购物。

sentences.en: But I don't think I got there without a few mistakes along the way, for sure.
sentences.zh: 但我相信我能走到今天，一路上肯定也犯过不少错误。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think we all do.
sentences.zh: 对，我想我们都会。

sentences.en: We all make some bad, bad spending choices.
sentences.zh: 我们都会做出一些糟糕透顶的消费选择。

sentences.en: But I think it's helpful.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这很有帮助。

sentences.en: Amy, you're bringing a lot of information to listeners, too, about things they can look for in their own shopping behaviors to help make them wiser consumers.
sentences.zh: 艾米，你也为听众带来了大量的信息，关于他们在自己的购物行为中可以注意哪些方面，从而帮助自己成为更明智的消费者。

sentences.en: And I think that's really important.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的非常重要。

sentences.en: So when dear knowledge you've gained, you're helping others become just more mindful of what they're spending, why they're spending.
sentences.zh: 所以通过你获得的知识，你正在帮助其他人对他们在买什么、为什么买有更多的觉察。

sentences.en: And I think that that does help everyone overall.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这确实对每个人都有整体的帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I hope so.
sentences.zh: 希望如此。

sentences.en: I enjoy doing it a lot.
sentences.zh: 我非常享受做这件事。

sentences.en: I really love my I love my research.
sentences.zh: 我真的很热爱我的——我热爱我的研究。

sentences.en: I love my work.
sentences.zh: 我热爱我的工作。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢您加入我们，亚罗博士。

sentences.en: This has been a really, really fascinating conversation.
